what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat HIV-1 infection in adults. It contains two different medicines that work together to lower the amount of HIV virus in your blood. Keeping the virus at a very low level helps protect your immune system and keeps you healthier. This medicine does NOT cure HIV, but it helps control it.
how_to_take: Take one tablet by mouth once a day, every day, at the same time each day. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or split it. Taking it at the same time each day helps it work its best. Never skip doses or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel well.
dosing: The usual dose for adults is ONE tablet taken by mouth ONCE daily. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not take more or less than instructed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — as long as it is within 12 hours of your usual time. If it has been more than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular scheduled time. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Call your doctor if you miss doses often.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in the original bottle with the cap tightly closed. Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the bottle.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT take rifampin, rifapentine, rifabutin, St. John's Wort, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, or phenytoin while on this medicine, as they can make it stop working. Avoid drinking alcohol in large amounts, as it can affect your liver and overall health. Do not share this medicine with anyone else. Remember, this medicine does not prevent passing HIV to others — always use safe sex practices and do not share needles.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, severe tiredness or weakness, unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, signs of depression or mood changes, thoughts of hurting yourself, swelling of your face or throat, skin rash, or any signs of an immune reaction. Also call your doctor if you notice changes in weight, fat redistribution (fat gaining in unusual places), numbness or tingling, or if you feel your medicine is not working.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working right away, but it may take a few weeks before you notice a difference in your lab results (such as your viral load and CD4 count). Most people see their viral load drop to very low or undetectable levels within 3 to 6 months. Continue taking it every day even if you feel fine — stopping or skipping doses can allow the virus to grow stronger and become resistant to the medicine.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of this medicine in pregnancy is not yet fully established. Breastfeeding is not recommended if you have HIV, because HIV can be passed to your baby through breast milk. Kidney or Liver Problems: Tell your doctor if you have any kidney or liver problems before starting this medicine, as dose adjustments may be needed. Older Adults: Older patients may need extra monitoring. Always tell your doctor about all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take.
